as_told.title: 1971 SALT-era language on coordinating with the Soviets over unknowns

plain: Pippa Malmgren, whose father Harald Malmgren was a presidential adviser, points on Jesse Michels's podcast to a 1971 agreement between the United States and the Soviet Union, which she calls the SALT treaty, a deal on limiting nuclear weapons. According to her, it contained "deconfliction" wording, meaning wording meant to stop either side from mistaking something for an attack. In the context of the conversation, she offers it as a hint that the two powers had to plan around things in the sky.
